betterCitation: Etty Hillesum, An Interrupted Life, the last diary entry, October 1942, p. 196 (trans. Arnold J. Pomerans, 1983)
reason: The verifier could not read the page; I could. Internet Archive full-text search over the Pantheon 1983 scans (interruptedlife00etty and interruptedlifed0000hill) returns the diary's closing line on the page itself: 'We should be willing to act as a balm for all wounds.' followed by the page number 196 and the heading LETTERS FROM WESTERBORK. The Washington Square Press 1985 printing (p. 243), the Triad 'Etty: A Diary 1941-43' (1985) and the Holt 1996 edition (p. 231) print the same sentence. So wording, translator (Pomerans) and edition hold, and the page is 196. Date: 'Etty Hillesum: For God and with God' gives 13 October 1942 as her last diary entry, while the British Library blog says 10 October; 'October 1942' is safe. shipped.js: not shipped; Hillesum at 2 of 3 (months 2 and 10), so allowed. Not banned, in scope, Diary tag right, publishable (the line itself carries no graphic content). Source leads with the name, no dash, 104 characters (112 with p. 196). THE NOTE MUST BE CORRECTED before it ships: it asserts, without a reading, that the complete edition renders the Dutch differently and that a line in capitals follows it in the manuscript. Coetsier (Etty Hillesum and the Flow of Presence, 2008) cites this same English wording to both the Dutch complete edition (p. 583) and the Eerdmans English complete edition (p. 550), which contradicts the note's first claim, and I found nothing to confirm the capitals. Replace it with what is known: 'The closing sentence of the diary as the 1983 selection prints it, p. 196. The Dutch reads Men zou een pleister op vele wonden willen zijn.' Nothing more.
